first_impression.reaction: Paros came up because a friend said it's Mykonos without the try-hard crowd. The opener is calm and gets straight to how to sort the island: 'The right one depends on your guest count, the ceremony you want (chapel, beach or terrace) and whether you would rather your guests sleep under the same roof.' That last bit is exactly our question with half the guests flying from Australia. No 'paradise', no 'dream day'. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Few Paros venues publish a wedding capacity, and the clearest figures belong to Petra Farm (a chapel for 120 and an event space for 150) and The Secret View (110 for a terrace ceremony, 120 for dinner).
journey.reaction: Straight away I know two places that definitely fit 60 to 90. And it admits the rest don't publish numbers instead of padding it out. That honesty is why I keep going.

journey.section: Paros wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: A table narrows the field. Only the venue can tell you what is free on your date, and under which house rules.
journey.reaction: Fair, but the table is mostly 'Not published' in the capacity and exclusive-use columns. Six of eight venues I can't actually rule in or out for 80 people from this page. That's the island's problem, not the writer's, but it means more homework for us.

journey.quote: For everyone else, ask whether the chapel hosts a religious, civil or symbolic ceremony before you fall for the setting.
journey.reaction: Neither of us is Orthodox, so this is the exact trap I'd have walked into: fall for a whitewashed chapel, then find out we can't actually marry in it. Glad it's said plainly.

journey.quote: Ask for current wedding terms, as that page dates from 2018.
journey.reaction: Small thing, but it tells me someone actually opened these pages and checked the dates. Same with Pyrgaki's 2020 page. That's the opposite of a copy-pasted listicle.

journey.quote: The farm limits itself to 10 weddings a year, and its team is on site to oversee every supplier for the whole rental period.
journey.reaction: This is the one I'm sending James. Ten a year means it won't feel like a conveyor belt, and a team on site overseeing suppliers speaks to my 'nobody accountable on the day' worry. Olive groves and a chapel for 120 also feels personal, not resort.
Then where do our 40-odd international guests sleep? If it's no rooms, how far are the nearest hotels and who's driving Nana up the hill?

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate
journey.quote: House rules are published: loud music stops at 2am, out of respect for the local villages, with a quieter after-party (an acoustic band, for example) possible.
journey.reaction: Love that this is spelled out. A real rule, a real reason, and a workaround. Plus shuttles organised by the venue and 24-hour access. Second one on our shortlist.

journey.section: A civil ceremony with the Municipality of Paros
journey.quote: The municipality does not publish the steps, documents, ceremony location or lead times for foreign couples.
journey.reaction: Honest, and lawyer brain respects that it doesn't pretend. But 'confidence the legal side is sorted' is one of our three goals, and right now the answer is 'ring a Greek municipality and an embassy'. I'd want to know who does that chasing for us.

journey.quote: An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: Clear and correctly hedged. The CNI and apostille bits are laid out in a way I could hand to Mum without explaining. Good section.

journey.quote: Paros Airport (PAS) is 9 km southwest of Parikia.
journey.reaction: Useful, and the 45-minute Athens hop is reassuring. But nothing on how long from the airport to Petra Farm or Golden Beach. That's still my number one worry: grandparents from the airport to the venue.

journey.quote: Build that into the arrival day for older guests.
journey.reaction: Someone has thought about our grandparents in a biometric queue after 24 hours of flying. Exactly the kind of insider logistics I'm looking for.

journey.quote: At the [Hellenic National Meteorological Service's Naxos station](http://oldportal.emy.gr/emy/en/climatology/climatology_city?perifereia=South%20Aegean&poli=Naxos), the mean monthly maximum is 22.1°C in May, 25.9°C in June, 27.1°C in July, 27.0°C in August, 25.1°C in September and 21.9°C in October.
journey.reaction: Finally a month-by-month view I can forward to Mum and Dad. With the rain days alongside, late May or September is suddenly an easy conversation.

journey.quote: Ask every venue on your shortlist these questions, and get the answers in writing:
journey.reaction: Copying this straight into our shared doc. Music cut-off, weather plan, minimum stay: the stuff we'd only think of after signing.

journey.section: Shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: That speaks directly to my hidden-costs fear, and with 'one person, start to finish' and AUD quotes it covers being handed around strangers too. Still doesn't tell me who's physically on Paros on the day.

unanswered_questions: Is there a real Paros (or Greece) wedding you've planned, with venue and date, that I can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests, half flying from Australia, which two or three of these eight would you shortlist?
Who chases the 'Not published' answers and the municipality's civil marriage requirements: us, or our Wedded Advisor?
How long is the drive from Paros Airport and Parikia port to each venue, and do you arrange guest transfers?
Where would guests stay for Petra Farm and The Secret View, and how far are those hotels?
Is our Wedded Advisor, or someone you are accountable for, physically on Paros on the wedding day?
would_share_with: James (partner): the Petra Farm and The Secret View entries, plus the at-a-glance table, to start a two-venue shortlist
Mum and Dad (contributing): the month-by-month temperatures and rain days, and the 'Steps for Australian couples' section
James again: the booking checklist, as the questions we send every venue

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=paros-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and 'fee agreed in writing before any work begins' takes the edge off. This is one of the better posts I've read, so it moves Wedded Wonderland up our list, but I'd still read another post or two and want to see a real wedding before I enquire.

top_3_changes: Give guests a sense of travel time from the airport and Parikia port to each area or venue (where venues publish it), so the 'grandparents from the airport' question isn't left at '9 km southwest of Parikia'.
For the no-rooms venues (Petra Farm, The Secret View, Monastiri), say where guests would typically base themselves, so couples with long-haul guests can judge the trade-off.
Make it clear in the secondary CTA or civil ceremony section that the 'Not published' answers and municipality steps are something the Wedded Advisor confirms, not homework left with the couple.
